resources.title: Sleuth Kit: filesystem analysis scenarios
resources.learn: Follow a string hit from unallocated space to its original disk block, inode and deleted filename; learn why byte offsets and filesystem units differ. Read Search first; treat the historic filesystem examples as concepts to adapt.
resources.offline: Save the page before departure. Reading needs no image; repeating commands needs a local disk image and installed Sleuth Kit. Example image names are illustrative, not bundled downloads.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Fetched official wiki and read Search, inode lookup and recovery examples. The old scenario mixes an extracted-image offset with an original-image dd command: use the blkcalc/blkcat sequence to understand the coordinate conversion; do not copy every line blindly.

resources.title: Autopsy Quick Start Guide
resources.learn: Create a single-user case, add a raw/E01 image, choose ingest modules, search keywords, inspect extracted browser activity and export an interesting file.
resources.offline: Save the guide including images. For hands-on work, stage a small local image and let ingest finish before boarding; avoid modules that need network services. Documentation is for 4.20.0, not a verified installed version.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read official case creation, data-source, ingest, analysis and example-use-case sections. No Autopsy instance was run.

resources.title: Volatility 3: Windows Tutorial
resources.learn: Understand plugin syntax and compare pslist with pstree to reconstruct processes and parent-child relationships in a Windows memory dump.
resources.offline: Save the page. Stage the memory image and resolve its symbols while online, then test the chosen commands offline: Windows symbol files may otherwise require Microsoft downloads. Volatility does not acquire memory.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read official syntax, pslist/pstree output and the automatic PDB/ISF download explanation. Did not download the example dump or run plugins.

resources.title: Introduction to Memory Forensics with Volatility 3
resources.learn: See the workflow from memory information to processes, handles, connections, extracted files and registry artifacts; use the official Windows tutorial for current command spelling.
resources.offline: Save using a permitted platform offline feature and confirm playback before departure; availability can depend on account and region. Save the companion notes at https://dfir.science/2022/02/Introduction-to-Memory-Forensics-with-Volatility-3 . Its practice-image link is optional and was not downloaded or tested.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read the creator companion page and inspected its HTML embedding this exact YouTube ID; YouTube fetch confirmed title and 2022 publication date but provided no transcript. Not watched. Companion command notes contain apparent typos including windows.registay and windows.dumpfile, so do not use them as a verbatim command sheet.

resources.title: Introduction to MFTECmd - NTFS MFT and Journal Forensics
resources.learn: Learn what $MFT and $UsnJrnl can reveal about file creation, deletion and renaming; follow MFTECmd CSV parsing at 10:33 and Timeline Explorer analysis at 13:00.
resources.offline: Save through a permitted platform offline feature and check playback. For practice, bring already extracted $MFT/$J files and the required Zimmerman tools/runtime. Skip the 06:00 KAPE acquisition chapter unless that separate tool is independently confirmed approved.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Fetched title, channel, description, chapter markers and transcript excerpts. The video demonstrates MFTECmd and Timeline Explorer and discusses a historical $LogFile limitation; no claim of current installed support. Not watched.

resources.title: qpdf: PDF inspection options
resources.learn: Move beyond visible page text: inspect PDF objects and attachments, distinguish compressed stream bytes from decoded stream data, and recognize the inspection-mode invocation.
resources.offline: Save the PDF Inspection section. Hands-on use needs installed qpdf and local sample PDFs; retain original files and use inspection operations. Unsupported stream filters may prevent decoding.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Fetched the full official CLI text and inspected PDF Inspection, show-object, raw-stream-data and filtered-stream-data passages; read the separate input/output rules.

resources.title: Chainsaw: searching and hunting Windows event logs
resources.learn: Search EVTX files by string or event field, then compare those results with Sigma-based hunting using a mapping file and time filters. Start with search before loading a large ruleset.
resources.offline: Save README examples and, for a local exercise, stage a small EVTX set plus matching rules and mapping files. Check the installed 2.16.5 help against the current README. No hosted backend is needed for the documented local-file workflow.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read upstream features and concrete search/hunt examples including Sigma mapping and CSV/JSON output. Did not run Chainsaw or validate the referenced sample logs. The README prose has a 4014/4104 typo; the displayed command uses 4104.

resources.title: SQLite command-line shell: inspect schema and records
resources.learn: Read Getting Started, dot-commands, output formats and Querying the database schema; use .tables and .schema before querying an unfamiliar artifact database.
resources.offline: Save these sections, not the whole manual as a study assignment. Use a local copy of a database and preserve any supplied WAL/SHM companions. This is SQLite CLI instruction, not deleted-record recovery or SQLCipher decryption.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read official startup, dot-command list, formatting and schema examples. Current documentation may include flags absent in the event installation; no installed CLI was tested.

caveats: Study times are curator estimates including note-taking, not measured video lengths.
Approval covers workbook rows; it does not guarantee functioning Kali installations or every tool mentioned by a tutorial. Existing per-tool documentation remains available in the input manifest.
No downloads, installs, video playback, practice-image execution or portal access were performed. Prepare and test local assets before flying.
Volatility 2 and 3 use different plugin/profile models. The core memory path is Volatility 3; do not apply it verbatim to the approved Kali Volatility 2 row.
Tutorial acquisition tools are not automatically approved. Work from supplied public practice artifacts; this curation does not expand the approved standalone application list.
search_notes: Used Exa search and fetch for official TSK/Autopsy docs, Volatility docs, creator videos, qpdf, Chainsaw and SQLite. Used a direct HTML read of the DFIRScience page to verify its exact embedded video ID.
Discarded the 13Cubed Volatility 3 Public Beta video as an outdated primary lesson; retained current official syntax with a later DFIRScience workflow video.
Discarded broad playlists, course aggregators, and duplicate Autopsy case-start videos to keep eight focused items.

Mobile, macOS, mailbox, browser-specific, credential and niche recovery tools intentionally remain reference-only. All assigned rows have a disposition; this is coverage accounting, not a claim that eight resources teach every tool.

The DFIRScience companion links a public Africa-DFIRCTF-2021-WK02 practice memory image. Availability, size and offline compatibility were not tested, so it is not promoted as a flight-ready practice exercise.
